issues.legal_issue: A premature suit for redemption cannot be continued merely because the claimant undertakes not to seek possession before the mortgage term expires.
material_facts: A suit seeking redemption was filed before the specified mortgage term expired.
The mortgage did not provide a right to redeem before the term expired, and the term was not a clog on the equity of redemption.
The claimant’s advocate stated that possession would not be sought before the stipulated expiry of the mortgage term.
The lower courts had dismissed the suit as premature, but the High Court remanded it for further proceedings on the basis of the undertaking.
issues.conclusion: The suit was premature and had to be dismissed; the undertaking not to take possession before the stipulated date did not permit the suit to continue.
issues.legal_principle: Ordinarily, absent a special condition entitling the mortgagor to redeem during the mortgage term, the right of redemption arises only when the specified term expires. A suit brought before then must fail. The Court relied on Seth Ganga Dhar v. Shankar Lal, which followed Bakhtawar Begum v. Husaini Khanam, and applied Gangadhar v. Shankar Lal, which held that a premature redemption suit must fail where the term was not a clog on redemption.

rule.if: redemption_suit and filed_before_redemption_due and no_early_redemption_right and mortgage_term_not_clog and undertaking_to_delay_possession

predicates.redemption_suit: A claimant brought a suit seeking redemption of mortgaged property.
predicates.filed_before_redemption_due: The claimant filed the suit before the specified redemption date.
predicates.no_early_redemption_right: The mortgage terms did not give the claimant a right to redeem before the specified term expired.
predicates.mortgage_term_not_clog: The mortgage term was not found to be a clog on the equity of redemption.
predicates.undertaking_to_delay_possession: The claimant’s advocate stated that possession would not be sought before the specified redemption date.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings a redemption suit before the specified date, has no right to redeem earlier, and the term is not a clog on redemption, an undertaking to delay possession does not prevent dismissal of the premature suit.

issues.legal_issue: An interlocutory remand order may be challenged in an appeal from the final judgment in the proceedings.
material_facts: The High Court made a remand order that did not terminate the proceedings.
Further proceedings took place following the remand, and a final decision was later appealed.
The appellants challenged the earlier remand order in their appeal from the later decision.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were entitled to challenge the interlocutory remand order in the appeal from the final decision; because the remand order was erroneous, the proceedings and orders consequent to it were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: An order of remand that does not terminate the proceedings is an interlocutory judgment and may be challenged in an appeal from the final order. The Court relied on Satyadhyan Ghosal v. Smt. Deorajin Debi and Kshitish Chandra Bose v. Commissioner of Ranchi, and also referred to Gangadhar v. Shankar Lal in support of allowing the challenge at that stage.

predicates.appeal_from_final_order: A party appealed from a final order in proceedings that had followed a remand.
predicates.earlier_interlocutory_remand: A court had earlier made a remand order that did not terminate the proceedings.

issues.definition: When a party appeals from a final order following an interlocutory remand, the party may challenge that remand order in the final appeal.
